questions.question:
A kubeconfig file is available at `/tmp/exam/1/kubeconfig`.

Extract the following information from it:

1. Write all kubeconfig context names to `/tmp/exam/1/contexts`, one per line.
2. Write the name of the current context to `/tmp/exam/1/current-context`.
3. Write the `client-certificate-data` of user `account-0027@internal`, base64-decoded, to `/tmp/exam/1/cert`.

Use `kubectl config` where practical.

verification.description: All three context names are listed in /tmp/exam/1/contexts
Current context is cluster-w200
The decoded client certificate is a valid PEM certificate

questions.question:
Install cert-manager with Helm in namespace `cert-manager` and configure a ClusterIssuer:

1. Create namespace `cert-manager`.
2. Install the Helm chart `jetstack/cert-manager` with release name `cert-manager` and `crds.enabled=true` into that namespace.
3. Edit `/tmp/exam/2/cluster-issuer.yaml` and add `crlDistributionPoints: ["http://example.com/crl"]` under `spec.selfSigned`.
4. Create the ClusterIssuer from that file.

The `jetstack` Helm repository is already available. cert-manager does not need to issue real certificates.

verification.description: Helm release cert-manager is installed in namespace cert-manager
The ClusterIssuer manifest contains the requested crlDistributionPoints
The cert-manager ClusterIssuer CRD is installed
ClusterIssuer course-issuer exists with the CRL distribution point

Scale the StatefulSet down to exactly one replica. Do not delete the StatefulSet.

questions.question:
Check all Pods in namespace `project-c13` and find the Pods that would probably be terminated first if the nodes run out of CPU or memory.

Write their names, one per line, to `/tmp/exam/4/pods-terminated-first.txt`.

Pods without CPU or memory requests/limits (QoS class `BestEffort`) are the first candidates.

verification.description: The answer file exists and is not empty
The file lists exactly the BestEffort Pods in project-c13

questions.question:
The application `api-gateway` used an external autoscaler and should now use a HorizontalPodAutoscaler.

Using the Kustomize configuration at `/tmp/exam/5/api-gateway`:

1. Remove the ConfigMap `horizontal-scaling-config` completely from the base and both overlays.
2. Add an HPA named `api-gateway` for Deployment `api-gateway` with min 2, max 4 replicas and 50% average CPU utilisation.
3. In the prod overlay the HPA must have max 6 replicas.
4. Apply the staging and prod overlays so the changes are reflected in the cluster.

The ConfigMaps already exist in the cluster and must also be removed from both namespaces.

verification.description: Both overlays build and no longer contain the horizontal-scaling-config ConfigMap
Staging HPA targets api-gateway with min 2, max 4 and 50% CPU
Prod HPA targets api-gateway with min 2, max 6 and 50% CPU
The ConfigMaps are gone from both namespaces

questions.question:
Create storage and a workload in namespace `project-t230`:

1. Create a PersistentVolume named `safari-pv` with capacity `2Gi`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce`, hostPath `/Volumes/Data`, and no `storageClassName`.
2. Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `safari-pvc` requesting `2Gi`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce`, and no `storageClassName`. It must bind to `safari-pv`.
3. Create a Deployment named `safari` using image `httpd:2-alpine` that mounts the PVC at `/tmp/safari-data`.

verification.description: PV safari-pv has 2Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /Volumes/Data and no storage class
PVC safari-pvc requests 2Gi, ReadWriteOnce, has no storage class and is Bound to safari-pv
Deployment safari mounts safari-pvc at /tmp/safari-data and is running

pod.sh uses kubectl top pod with container usage

questions.question:
In namespace `project-tiger`, create a DaemonSet named `ds-important`:

1. Image `httpd:2-alpine`.
2. Labels `id=ds-important` and `uuid=18426a0b-5f59-4e10-923f-c0e078e82462` on the DaemonSet and its Pods.
3. Pods request `10m` CPU and `10Mi` memory.
4. Pods must run on every node, including the control-plane node.

The control-plane node is tainted with `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule`.

verification.description: DaemonSet spec has the required labels, image, requests and control-plane toleration
Exactly one ds-important Pod runs on every Ready node

questions.question:
In namespace `project-tiger`, create a Deployment named `deploy-important`:

1. 3 replicas.
2. The Deployment and its Pods have label `id=very-important`.
3. First container `container` uses image `nginx:1-alpine`.
4. Second container `container2` uses image `registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10`.
5. Only one Pod may run on each worker node. Use `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` with pod anti-affinity or topology spread constraints.

The control-plane node is tainted. Because there are two worker nodes and three replicas, the third Pod should remain Pending.

verification.description: Deployment has the required labels, replicas, containers and hostname scheduling rule
Two Pods run on distinct worker nodes and the third is Pending
No deploy-important Pod runs on the control-plane node

questions.question:
Project r500 wants to replace an Ingress with Gateway API resources. The old Ingress is available at `/tmp/exam/13/ingress.yaml` and a Gateway named `main` already exists in namespace `project-r500`.

Create an HTTPRoute named `traffic-director` that:

1. Replicates the Ingress routes: `/desktop` to Service `web-desktop` port 80 and `/mobile` to Service `web-mobile` port 80, for host `r500.gateway`.
2. Adds path `/auto`: if the `User-Agent` header is exactly `mobile`, forward to `web-mobile`; otherwise forward to `web-desktop`.

No Gateway controller runs in this cluster, so validation is performed on the HTTPRoute spec.

verification.description: HTTPRoute traffic-director references Gateway main and hostname r500.gateway
Desktop and mobile prefix routes target the correct Services
The /auto mobile rule matches User-Agent exactly and targets web-mobile
The /auto catch-all rule targets web-desktop and comes after the header rule

questions.question:
After a security incident, create a NetworkPolicy named `np-backend` in namespace `project-snake`.

The policy must allow the `backend-*` Pods only to:

1. Connect to `db1-*` Pods on port `1111`.
2. Connect to `db2-*` Pods on port `2222`.

Use the `app` Pod labels. All other egress from `backend-*` Pods must be denied.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy selects app=backend and declares only Egress
Two egress rules allow db1:1111 and db2:2222
Allowed traffic to db1:1111 and db2:2222 works
Traffic to vault:3333 and db2:1111 is blocked

questions.question:
Update the CoreDNS configuration:

1. Back up the existing CoreDNS ConfigMap to `/tmp/exam/16/coredns_backup.yaml` so it can be restored quickly.
2. Update CoreDNS so `SERVICE.NAMESPACE.custom-domain` resolves the same as `SERVICE.NAMESPACE.cluster.local`, in addition to it.
3. Restart CoreDNS and confirm it is healthy.

You can test with a `busybox:1.36` Pod using `nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.custom-domain`.

verification.description: The CoreDNS ConfigMap backup exists
The CoreDNS Corefile includes custom-domain alongside cluster.local
CoreDNS is rolled out and ready
